nature: Bounded responsive CSS fix for the IMP-10 F-1 narrow-viewport horizontal overflow, with a focused CSS regression suite, rebuilt bundles (read back), and a re-run of the full 32-step scratch browser qualification against the fixture mockup bundle. Zero live calls, zero consumer changes, zero dependency upgrades, zero commits.

root_cause.reported: IMP-10 attributed the 375px overflow to .calendar-impact__row (fixed grid tracks 116px minmax(160px,1fr) 64px 70px 92px 124px auto).
root_cause.corrected_finding: The measured document scrollWidth 799px could not come from calendar-impact alone (its min-content is ~674px). Re-measurement pinned the dominant overflow to the allocator table grid .queue__cols/.qrow (tracks 3px minmax(0,1fr) 128px 256px minmax(348px,auto) ≈ 783px min + gaps = 799px), with .band header flex rows spilling ~24px past the viewport. All three are the same defect class: fixed-wide grid/flex tracks with no @media (max-width:767px) treatment.
evidence: Before fix: scrollWidth 799 vs clientWidth 375 at 375x812 (#sequenced); .qrow__actions right edge 799.
After fix: scrollWidth 375 == clientWidth 375; zero elements wider than the viewport (probe wideCount 0).

css_change.location: inside the existing @media (max-width: 767px) block (after .execution__cards, before .main), the same breakpoint the rail/execution/dock narrow rules use
css_change.desktop_impact: none — no base rules touched; desktop-untouched guards assert the base .calendar-impact__row (7 tracks) and .queue__cols/.qrow (5 tracks) declarations are unchanged

desktop calendar-impact grid untouched (7 tracks + auto)
